title: Detailed lens modeling and kinematics of the submillimeter galaxy G09v1.97: An analysis of CO, H<SUB>2</SUB>O, H<SUB>2</SUB>O<SUP>+</SUP>, and dust continuum emission
question: Constrain the ongoing processes, source-plane morphology, and kinematics (disk versus merger) in the z = 3.63 gravitationally lensed submillimeter galaxy H-ATLAS J083051.0+013224 (G09v1.97) using high angular resolution dust continuum, CO(6-5), H2O, and H2O+ emission.

data.sensitivity: Continuum: 0.02 mJy/beam; CO(6-5): 0.19 mJy/beam; H2O: 0.50 mJy/beam; H2O+: 0.13 mJy/beam

what.value: Lens galaxy spectroscopic redshifts (z = 0.636 and z = 1.002), initial lens offsets and Einstein radii, total infrared luminosity L_IR = (1.4 +/- 0.7) x 10^13 L_odot, and expected emission region mask

evidence.quote: The SMG G09v1.97 is lensed by two galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts of $z = 0.636$ and $z = 1.002$, visible in optical wavelengths (cite: Yang19).

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97
evidence.quote: G09v1.97 has been previously shown to be one of the most luminous dusty star-forming galaxies in the high-redshift universe with a total infrared luminosity of $L_{\mathrm{IR}} = (1.4 \pm 0.7) \times 10^{13} L_{\odot}$ (cite: Yang19).

Imaging of the calibrated data was performed in CASA using the tclean task, cleaning in the region of expected emission using the mask encompassing the region of emission for the deep continuum and CO(6–5) emission images reported in (cite: Yang19).

what.value: Initial priors/ranges for lens (x, y) offset and Einstein radius

evidence.quote: The ($x, y$) offset and Einstein radius were allowed to vary around previously reported values from (cite: Yang19) and (cite: Maresca22).

what.value: Conversion ratio between CO(6–5) and CO(1–0) emission from LVG CO SLED modeling, and helium contribution of 36%

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97
evidence.quote: We use the conversion ratio between the CO(6–5) and CO(1–0) emission based on single component large velocity gradient (LVG) modeling of the observed CO spectral line energy distribution (SLED) performed in (cite: Yang17)

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97
evidence.quote: Assuming $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 0.8$ (cite: Downes98) and a helium contribution of 36% (cite: Yang17), we obtain a gas mass in the region of CO(6–5) emission of $M_{\mathrm{gas}} = (1.8 \pm 0.74) \times 10^{10}$M$_{\odot}$.

recipe.goal: Measure image-plane continuum flux, extract line spectra, fit line profiles, and compute moment maps and line luminosities
recipe.method: Extract continuum flux and molecular line spectra from the expected emission region of Yang19; fit asymmetric line profiles with double Gaussian profiles; compute moment-0 and moment-1 maps (clipping <3 sigma in moment-1); calculate line luminosities using Solomon97 formula.
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_Lambda = 0.7, Omega_m = 0.3

recipe.goal: Perform parametric gravitational lens modeling on visibilities
recipe.method: Fit two foreground lens galaxies as single isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) mass profiles and the background source as a single linear Sérsic profile directly on the interferometric visibilities in PyAutoLens; optimize the lens mass model on dust continuum first, then fix the lens mass model to fit CO(6-5), H2O, and H2O+ emission.
key_parameters: Lens redshifts fixed at z = 0.626 (or 0.636 in text) and z = 1.002; 1000 posterior samples for magnification error
assumptions: Two SIE lens mass profiles and a single Sérsic source profile

recipe.goal: Perform non-parametric pixelated source-plane reconstructions and reconstruct the de-magnified CO(6-5) spectral cube
recipe.method: Using the continuum-optimized lens mass model, reconstruct source-plane emission on a magnification-weighted adaptive Voronoi pixel mesh with constant regularization in PyAutoLens; bin CO(6-5) into 50 km/s channels, reconstruct each bin non-parametrically, and interpolate onto a square pixel grid to form a de-magnified spectral cube; compute source-plane error maps from lens posterior sampling and visibility covariance matrix (via CASA STATWT).
key_parameters: Circular region of radius 1.5 arcsec (11 kpc); CO(6-5) cube spectral resolution ~50 km/s; static source-plane beam of 0.035'' x 0.027'' (5 pixels per beam); 1000 samples for sigma_l; 100 samples for pixelized magnification error
assumptions: Static source-plane beam defined as theta_maj/sqrt(mu) x theta_min/sqrt(mu) with 5 pixels per beam; Gaussian distribution of lens model parameters over 1000 samples

recipe.goal: Model source-plane CO(6-5) kinematics and classify disk vs. merger
recipe.method: Fit tilted rings to the de-magnified source-plane CO(6-5) spectral cube using 3DBarolo (first with PA and inclination free, then fixing them to their averages and refitting); calculate PVsplit parameters from the major-axis PV diagram to test disk vs. merger classification.
key_parameters: Smooth & Search masking with 3 sigma cut; 11 rings with radial separation 0.0138'' (theta_maj / 2.5); center fixed via 2D-Gaussian fit to moment-0 map; fixed i = 50 deg and PA = 6.7 deg
assumptions: Static source-plane beam of 0.035'' x 0.027''; V_rot in the outermost ring approximates V_max

recipe.goal: Derive physical properties: SFR, dynamical mass, gas mass, gas mass fraction, and depletion time
recipe.method: Calculate SFR from L_IR and from CO(6-5) emission; fit source-plane CO(6-5) spatial extent to derive Sigma_SFR; calculate dynamical mass from outermost 3DBarolo ring (Vc = 386 km/s, r = 1.07 kpc); convert CO(6-5) to CO(1-0) using LVG modeling from Yang17 to derive gas mass, gas mass fraction, and depletion time.
assumptions: Chabrier IMF; SFR ~ 10^-10 L_IR [L_odot]; alpha_CO = 0.8 (with error incorporating range 0.8-4.0); helium contribution of 36%; CO(6-5) to CO(1-0) ratio from Yang17 LVG modeling; CO(6-5) and CO(7-6) emission are very similar

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97
evidence.quote: This implies a depletion time (defined as $t_{\rm dep} = M_{\rm gas}/\mathrm{SFR}$) for G09v1.97 of $13 \pm 8$ Myr, lower than the value found for G09v1.97 by (cite: Yang17) but within the error range.

score_reason: Both ALMA project codes, main calibration/imaging parameters, lens model best-fit parameters, and kinematic modeling settings are clearly documented, and public tools (CASA, PyAutoLens, 3DBarolo) are used. Some low-level parameters (exact clean/extraction mask coordinates, line-free channels, cell sizes, and PyAutoLens regularization coefficients in text) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the analysis uses standard open-source packages (CASA, PyAutoLens, 3DBarolo), and the main conclusions rely on well-defined numeric outputs (fluxes, lens Einstein radii and magnifications, V_max/sigma, and M_dyn).
